description: We're a multidisciplinary team of students at UNIZAR, ​pursuing master's degrees in Robotics and in AI & Computational Engineering, and​ completing bachelor's degrees in Mechanical Engineering and in Finance & Accounting. We love tackling challenges with creativity and innovation, and we enjoy combining our different perspectives to find original solutions.

details:
What it does and how it works

Orbital Mission is a didactic, cooperative 3D game where one to four players design, manage and simulate a complete space mission. Players pick a difficulty and a destination (Moon or Mars), each with its own mass, budget and science limits, then work through four phases in a shared 3D mission-control room. Each player takes a role with its own mini-games:

  • Mechanic: assembles and inspects the rocket in 3D and prepares the launch.
  • Engineer: plans trajectories on an orbital whiteboard using the vis-viva equation, the rocket equation and Kepler’s third law.
  • Scientist: chooses instruments and tests materials under thermal stress.
  • Program Manager: splits a limited budget across departments and approves decisions.

The team takes shared decisions at a holographic table, guided by A.R.I.A., an AI assistant that explains each task and its consequences. The mission ends with a simulated launch that shows how their choices played out.

Benefits and intended impact

Budget, mass, power, orbit and materials compete within one mission, so no single answer is correct and every decision has visible consequences. Students practise systems thinking, teamwork and learning from failure, and are inspired to see themselves in space engineering.

Creativity

Players work inside a living mission-control room, and roles are interdependent, so no one succeeds alone. Orbital mechanics and material limits are learned through hands-on mini-games, not text.

Factors we considered

Accessibility for beginners (difficulty levels, a mentor assistant, gradual concepts), realistic constraints, balanced roles, replayability through different destinations, and a clear link between each decision and its outcome.

Tools and technologies

  • Vercel
  • Canva
  • Google AI Studio
  • Gemini
  • Claude
